blocks.value: Asset Allocation means dividing your money across different types of investments instead of investing everything in one place.
Imagine This: A healthy meal contains rice, vegetables, dal and fruits. Eating only one food every day isn't balanced. Your investments should also be balanced across different asset classes.
Common asset classes include Stocks, Mutual Funds, Fixed Deposits, Gold, Bonds and Cash. The right mix depends on your age, financial goals and ability to handle risk.
A young investor may choose 70% Stocks, 20% Mutual Funds and 10% Cash, while someone nearing retirement may prefer a more conservative allocation.
Don't ask 'Which investment is best?' Ask 'What combination of investments is best for me?'

blocks.question: What is Asset Allocation?
choices: Dividing investments across different asset classes.
